title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics · Chapter 5 Arithmetic Progressions (NCERT reprint 2026-27)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions modelled on question types that have repeated in CBSE board papers 2022-2026 and the Sample Question Papers 2024-25 to 2026-27. They are practice for readiness, not predictions of what will appear in any exam.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number (negative allowed). No calculator.

patterns.T1: Find d / a term / which term / number of terms
patterns.T2: kth term from the end / middle term

S1.name: What makes an AP: common difference
S1.tip: An AP adds the same d every time. d = later term − earlier term (6, 3, 0 has d = −3). Check every difference.

S2.name: The nth term: a term, which term, is it a term
S2.tip: an = a + (n − 1)d. Which term is x: solve for n, and n must be a positive whole number. Count terms with the formula, not (l − a)/d.

S3.name: Two terms given; terms from the end; middle term
S3.tip: Two terms given: write both as a + (n − 1)d and solve. am − ak = (m − k)d. kth from the end = (n − k + 1)th term; count terms first.

S4.name: Three terms in AP (2b = a + c)
S4.tip: a, b, c in AP exactly when 2b = a + c. Three unknown terms: take a − d, a, a + d (their sum is 3a).

S5.name: Sum of n terms
S5.tip: Sn = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d], or n/2 (a + l) when the last term is known. 1 + 2 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2.

S6.name: Sum given: find n (incl. the double answer)
S6.tip: Sum given and n unknown gives a quadratic in n. Two positive answers can both be right when some terms cancel (sum 0).

S7.name: Sn given as a formula in n
S7.tip: an = Sn − S(n − 1) and the first term is S1. Then d = a2 − a1.

S8.name: Two conditions on terms or sums
S8.tip: Two conditions (two sums, or two terms) give a pair of linear equations in a and d: solve them, then answer the question.

S9.name: Word problems and case studies
S9.tip: Spot the AP (simple interest, a fixed yearly rise, rows, exterior angles adding to 360°). One value → an; a total → Sn.

questions.question: The common difference of the AP 11, 7, 3, −1, … is:
Which list is an AP?
The AP 7, 13, 19, … continues. What is the 5th term?
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: 1 − (−3) = 4, 5 − 1 = 4, 9 − 5 = 4: A is true, and R is the reason it is an AP.
questions.reason: In an AP, the difference between consecutive terms is constant.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
